_doc: Named NPCs. Optional `birthday` {month 1..12, day 1..30} gives a named NPC a yearly birthday (FOLK-022; without it a named NPC has none, generated villagers get a hashed one) optional `player_birthday_line` (FOLK-029, <=160 chars, {player}) is what they say on the PLAYER's birthday instead of the shared folk_greetings.player_birthday pick, and optional `birthday_line` (<=160 chars, {player}) is what they say that day instead of the shared folk_greetings.birthday pool. Optional `festival_lines` (FOLK-025) {festival world-event id (festival: true in world_events.json): line (<=160 chars, {player})} is what they say when you chat during that festival in their region, once per festival per year (birthdays win), instead of the shared family.json folk_greetings.festival pool. Optional `taught_dish_line` (COOK-003, <= 160 chars, must contain {dish}) is what a friend who taught you a dish (a `learn_dish` lesson) says in their next chat within 14 days of the first time you cook it, once per dish, +3 favor. Optional `player_birthday_gift` (FOLK-030) {item (items.json id), count 1..3} is handed over with their own player_birthday_line (same once-a-year flag). Optional `lessons` [{tier (index into family.json folk_tiers, >= 1, strictly rising, max 2), text (<=220 chars, {name}/{player}), effects (only learn_recipe, learn_dish (COOK-001, a taught home meal), learn_technique, profession_xp, attributes 1..2, dao_insight, practice_days 1..10, items)}] are taught once, one a day per NPC, when you talk at that tier (FOLK-020). Each becomes a CharacterData at session start and lives on: it ages, cultivates off-screen (if 'cultivates') at its region's qi density times 'diligence' (fraction of days spent cultivating, default 0.3), attempts breakthroughs and can die of old age. realm is a realm id; roots map element ids to purity (omit to roll randomly); attributes default to 10. region/pos/size/color place the NPC in the world. gender (optional) is a data/names.json gender; surname/given_name are optional (name stays the display name). NPCs generated at runtime (Npcs.spawn) have no entry here. dialogue is a file id in data/dialogue/. likes/dislikes (GIFT-001, optional): lists of item ids or item tags; a gift matching a like is worth family.json acquaintance.gift_like_mult times as much, a dislike costs gift_dislike_favor (a dislike wins when both match). Validated against items.json ids and tags. deed_context (optional) also offers deeds from data/deeds.json. bloodline (optional) is a data/bloodlines.json id the NPC carries (and may pass to children). hunter (WILD-017, optional bool): the NPC leads their region's village hunt (VillageHunt.hunter_of): named in the notice, +2 more favor on a win. Optional `spots` (FOLK-017, named NPCs with a region): {work, market, rain, festival: [x, y] inside the region map; rest_weekday: a weekday name}. Folk.spot_for picks where the NPC stands today: a running festival (the festival spot, else near the region festival_square) > rain or storm (rain) > rest_weekday (stays at pos) > a market day of the region (market) > work > pos; a missing spot falls through. Optional top-level "scenes" (FOLK-013): [{id (unique), npc (a named npc id or "any_villager"), min_favor (a family.json folk_tiers min), text (1-3 sentences, {name} = the villager), gift (optional items.json id), weather (optional non-empty list of Weather kinds: clear, cloudy, rain, snow, fog, storm; the scene plays only on such a day in the region you stand in, FOLK-021)}]; shown once, at most one a day, when you talk to the villager. Optional top-level "errands" (GUIDE-003) feed the journal: {npc: named npc id, asked_flag, done_flag, text}; listed while the asked flag is set and the done flag is not.

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, another year on your road. Sit a while; an old man is allowed to say he is glad you were born.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {player}, the drums fade and the lanterns burn down, but a walk beside you is what I will keep from {festival}. Old men hoard such things.

festival_lines.lantern_festival: {player}, on lantern night we set old grudges on the water. Mine sank long ago; light one with me and watch it go.
festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: {player}, sixty festivals and I still cannot paddle in time. Come, beat the drum with me.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}, another year on these old bones, and the tea is still hot. Sit with me.

lessons.text: {name} sits you down in the lee of the shrine wall and teaches you to count your breath until the counting stops. "Slow is not weak, child."
{name} says nothing for a long while, then lets you hear what the breath sounds like when it is truly even. "There. Keep that."

npcs.name: Elder Mo
npcs.title: Retired Cultivator

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, it is your birthday! Grandmother says I may not bake, so I made you a riddle instead. Many happy returns!
npcs.taught_dish_line: You made {dish}, the way I showed you? Did the steam come out slow? Grandmother says that is the only secret. Was it good? Tell me it was good!

festival_lines.lantern_festival: {player}! I wrote a riddle for the lantern game and nobody has solved it. You try! No, wait, don't tell Grandmother the answer.
festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: {player}! Did you try the rice dumplings? I wrapped the sweet ones myself, so don't scowl.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}! Do you know what day it is? Grandmother made too much, so you are staying to eat.

lessons.text: {name} shows you how she steams eggs and well water slow and low until the custard shivers like a pond, then sends you home with a bowl of broth.
{name} lifts a hot lid and shows you Grandmother's honey egg cake, every fold of it. "Don't tell anyone how little honey. Now it's yours too."

npcs.name: Xiao Ling
npcs.title: Childhood Friend

npcs.player_birthday_line: Hm. {player}. Birthday, I hear. Another year and you are still standing. Good. Keep at it.
npcs.taught_dish_line: Hm. Word is you cooked {dish}. Did you let it rest before you cut it? ...Good. A hunter who wastes no meat will never go hungry. Keep at it.

festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: Hm. Loud, this boat business. But the river hasn't run so bright in years.
festival_lines.lantern_festival: Hm. Paper lights on the river. The deer would not understand it. I do. Stand by me a while, {player}.

npcs.birthday_line: Hm. {player}. The years pass like deer, quiet and gone. Stay for the fire tonight.

lessons.text: {name} crouches by the trail and shows you how to read a track and place your feet so the leaves stay silent, then roasts the boar you both carried home and shows you how to crackle the skin.
{name} walks you along the ridge at dusk, correcting your stance twice a step, until you move through the brush like a drifting shadow.

npcs.name: Hunter Ma
npcs.title: Village Hunter

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a birthday? Then take the first dew-grass of the morning. It is the freshest thing I own, and you earned it.
npcs.taught_dish_line: The forest told me you made {dish}. Of course it did. I hope you drank it warm, with no hurry; a cup left to cool teaches nothing.
npcs.birthday_line: Oh, {player}, you remembered? The forest gave me a good year. Have some tea, it is only leaf and kindness.

lessons.text: {name} copies out the way she mends torn channels with a simple pill, brushing the lines dry with her sleeve.
{name} presses a frostbell blossom into your palm. "Two of these, steeped slow, and no summer fever lasts. Nobody sells this; I kept it for a friend."

npcs.name: Herbalist Lan
npcs.title: Herb Gatherer

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, I hear it is your birthday. Information costs, but this I give free: you are one year richer in days. Spend them well.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {festival} with you, {player}, and I forgot to count a single coin. Do not spread that around; it ruins my name.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: Mid-Autumn, {player}: the one night I haggle for pleasure, not profit. Take a moon cake. No, no charge. Do not tell the others.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}. Even brokers are born, it seems. I will not charge you for today's gossip. Only today.
npcs.name: Broker Qian
npcs.title: Information Broker

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a year older? Then your blade has had a year to learn you. Drink with me; the road can wait one evening.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {festival}. I do not usually stay for such days. I stayed, {player}. Do not make me say why.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Qingming. I sweep one grave each spring and name no one aloud. Sit, {player}; the cold dumplings are decent this year.

npcs.birthday_line: Another year, another road. {player}, sit. A sword is a poor thing to celebrate with, but I have wine.
npcs.name: Yun Feng
npcs.title: Wandering Swordsman

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, happy birthday. No pill buys another year, I have tried. But the tea I brewed you is warm, and that is something.
npcs.festival_memory_line: I still taste {festival} on my tongue, {player}. Whatever we ate, it was better shared. I am writing it in my recipe notes.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: {player}, I put a pinch of osmanthus in this year's moon cakes. Not medicine, I swear. Taste, and tell me the moon is brighter.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}, how did you know? Careful: a gift on the right day tastes sweeter than any pill I have brewed.

lessons.text: {name} lets you watch a full batch from first heat to last, and writes the settling of the clear-heart pill on a slip for you.
{name} taps the rim of the cauldron. "Healers' pills are patience. Here is how I draw the visceral mending pill, and why I never rush the fire."

npcs.name: Hua Qingyi
npcs.title: Wandering Alchemist

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}... they say today is yours. I do not do gifts. Take this: for one day, I will not mention the cost of anything.
npcs.birthday_line: Hmph. {player}. Do not look so pleased with yourself; you knowing the day means nothing. ...Stay anyway.
npcs.name: Xue Yao
npcs.title: Blood Lotus Disciple

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, your birthday, is it? Another ring on the pine. Sit; the clouds are good today and I have nobody else to tell.
npcs.festival_memory_line: I came down the mountain for {festival} and was glad of it, {player}. Company is a medicine I had forgotten to take.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Qingming brings visitors to my mountain. Most ask for wisdom; you have brought dumplings. Sit, {player}, you are the wise one.

npcs.birthday_line: A birthday, {player}? At my age they come like mountain mist. Still, it is good that someone climbs up to see me.
npcs.name: Hermit Gu
npcs.title: Retired Azure Cloud Elder

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}! Birthday, eh? Hee. Everything on my cart is half price today. Half of a fair price, that is. Don't tell the dead.
npcs.birthday_line: Ehe. {player} remembers the day the old peddler crawled out of the mud. Have a dry corner of my skiff.
npcs.name: Peddler Hei
npcs.title: Corpse Peddler

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, I heard it was your birthday. The sect forbids gifts between disciples, so this is only a feather I happened to find.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {player}! I am still smiling about {festival}. My seniors asked who I laughed with, and I said: a friend.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: {player}! The elders fly kites for the dead today. Mine is crooked, but I think my senior would have laughed at it.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}! The sect forgets such days, but you did not. I will practise my sword twice as long tomorrow.
npcs.name: Bai Qingwu
npcs.title: Azure Cloud Inner Disciple

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}. Today is your day, the ledgers say. I note it. I note everything. ...Happy birthday. That I do not note.
npcs.festival_memory_line: ...{festival} was loud, and I did not mind. That is your doing, {player}. Thank you for asking me along.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: ...The moon is full and the stalls are loud. I like it better than silence tonight, {player}. Take a lantern.

npcs.birthday_line: ...Today, yes. Few notice. Take a seat, {player}; I will not ask what you want. Not today.
npcs.name: Shen Wuya
npcs.title: Hollow-Eyed Broker

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a birthday is a small gate that opens once a year. Walk through it lightly. The Dao will wait for you on the other side.
npcs.festival_memory_line: A thousand peaks, and the sweetest hour of the season was {festival} at your side, {player}. Come, let an old man say thanks.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Every spring I count the names we have lost and the young ones we gained. Fly a kite with me, {player}; they climb higher than I do.

npcs.birthday_line: Another spring over a thousand peaks, {player}. The young ones hide gifts behind their backs; you may do the same.
npcs.name: Patriarch Lin
npcs.title: Founding Patriarch of the Azure Cloud Sect

npcs.player_birthday_line: Heh heh, {player}. Another year survived! The lanterns burn brighter for you tonight. I told them to. They obey me. Mostly.
npcs.birthday_line: Kekeke. {player}, you count my years? Then pour a cup for the ghosts, and one for me.
npcs.name: Old Monster Gui
npcs.title: Ghost-Lantern Old Monster

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, birthday! I could not find a cloud thick enough to wrap you a gift, so you have my good wishes and this warm pill.
npcs.birthday_line: The clouds were kind this morning, {player}, and now you are too. Even an alchemist can be pleased by a small gift.
npcs.name: Ye Zhuoran
npcs.title: Cloud-Walking Alchemist

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}. Another year is another skull you have not yet become. Be glad. I raise a cup, which is more than I do for most.
npcs.birthday_line: Hah. {player}, a skull for every year, they say. You bring something less grim? Then you are welcome at my fire.
npcs.name: Xuan Moying
npcs.title: Hundred-Skull Lord

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a year gone like a sword's flash. Do not mourn it. Stand, draw, and let this new year be sharper than the last.
npcs.birthday_line: I walk, I forget the date, and someone remembers it for me. Thank you, {player}. The road is lighter today.
npcs.name: Lan Zhiyuan
npcs.title: Wandering Sword-Saint

npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, happy birthday. A year is a fine stone to set in the wall of a life. Mind that you lay it straight, and lay it well.
npcs.birthday_line: {player}, the mountains have waited a long time for me to turn a year older. Sit; the mending can wait one day.
npcs.name: Wen Qingxu
npcs.title: Mountain-Mending Sage

errands.text: Elder Mo asked for 6 Spirit Herbs (the slope above Qingshi Village).
Herbalist Lan asked for 5 Qi Condensing Grass (Herb Patch, Misty Forest).
Hua Qingyi asked for 4 Qi Gathering Pills you made yourself.
Hermit Gu asked for 3 Cold Iron (the crystal vein, Azure Peak).
Peddler Hei asked for 3 Purple Cloud Mushrooms (Corpse-Lily Bog).
Patriarch Lin asked for 3 Ice Soul Flowers (Frost Ledge, Azure Peak).
Old Monster Gui asked for 3 Blood Ginseng (Corpse-Lily Bog, Withered Bone Marsh).
Ye Zhuoran asked for 3 Cloud Mist Orchids (Thunder-Struck Terraces, Myriad Peaks Ridge).
Bai Qingwu asked for 3 Nine-Leaf Soul Grass (Cloud-Sea Orchid Terraces, Azure Peak).
Shen Wuya asked for 2 Star Silver (Meteor Crater Field, Fallen Star Market).
Wen Qingxu asked for 2 Soul Infant Fruit (Thunder-Struck Terraces, Myriad Peaks Ridge).
Xuan Moying asked for a Soul Severing Lotus (it grows only where Nascent Soul cultivators can pick it).

scenes.text: {name} leads you to the rope swing behind her family's house, grey with rain now. "We were smaller than the knots, then," she laughs, and pushes you once, as she used to.
{name} insists you stay for supper. Nothing is said about why; the bowl is simply set down in front of you, full.
{name} pours you tea and, for once, does not lecture. "I spent sixty years chasing the heavens," the old cultivator says. "Sit. The kettle teaches patience better than I ever did."
{name} shows you a pale scar across the wrist and tells how it was earned, and what it cost a friend. "Do not repeat my mistakes. Make your own, smaller ones."
{name} hangs a paper lantern at her gate and writes your name beside hers on it. "For a good road," she says, a little pink, and presses a second lantern into your hands.
{name} walks you along the ridge path and shows how he sets a snare: patient hands, no hurry. "The wood tells you everything, if you stop talking," he grunts, and hands you a strip of smoked meat.
{name} lets you hold his old bow, the grip worn smooth by twenty winters. "I never lent it to anyone," he mutters, then nods once, which from him is a speech.
{name} sees you passing and calls up from the ladder. You hold it steady while the thatch is patched, and nobody mentions payment, only a nod of thanks.
{name} tells you how the village looked before the stone road: wolves in the barley and a sky full of crows. "We got by," they say. "People do."
{name} presses a bundle into your arms at the lane's end. "You came when the well ran dry and when the fever came. This is the least of it."
{name} brings a lamp and sits with you through the dark hours, saying little. At dawn the lamp is trimmed and the tea is hot: that is how friends are made here.
